title: Organisation to person engagement
summary: An organisation (a brand, studio or agency) books one individual for a single engagement: for example, a brand books a photographer for a campaign. The organisation signs through an authorised representative.
notice: Draft for review — not legal advice. A UK solicitor reviews this template before any real member signs.

clauses.text: This agreement is between [[engager]], an organisation that books and pays, and [[provider]], an individual who does the work.
[[Engager]] signs through a representative who confirms they have authority to bind it. SnapLink checks that authority when they sign.
[[Provider]] works as an independent contractor in business on their own account, not as an employee or worker of [[engager]].
Each party confirms, when signing, that they are 18 or over. SnapLink keeps this confirmation with their signature record.
The terms are fixed when the first party signs. Any change needs a new version signed by both parties; the earlier version is kept unchanged.
[[Provider]] will carry out {{engagement_summary}} with reasonable care and skill, as this agreement describes.
[[Engager]] will give [[provider]] the information and access they reasonably need to do the work, in good time.
The work takes place at {{venue}}, unless both parties agree a change in writing through SnapLink.
Whoever controls the venue makes sure it is safe to work in and tells the other party about any known hazard before the start.
The work is on {{engagement_date}}, from {{start_time}} to {{finish_time}}.
Work beyond the agreed hours happens only if both parties agree it at the time, including the rate for it, and that agreement is recorded through SnapLink.
[[Engager]] will pay [[provider]] {{fee}} ({{rate_basis}}).
A deposit of {{deposit}} (£0 means none) is due when both parties have signed. The balance is due within {{payment_days}} days of the work being completed.
[[Provider]] is {{vat_status}}.
Each party supplies the equipment and materials this agreement gives to them, and looks after their own equipment.
Travel and other expenses are paid only where this agreement, or a later agreement recorded through SnapLink, says so, against receipts.
Where the work produces material protected by copyright, its creator keeps the copyright. Any licence to use it is set out in this agreement, and any other use needs the creator’s written consent.

Nothing in this agreement assigns copyright unless a clause says so expressly, names what is assigned and states the fee for it. An assignment takes effect only when the creator has signed this agreement.
Moral rights cannot be assigned. They are waived only where a clause says so expressly and the creator has signed this agreement.
Each party follows the health and safety rules that apply at the venue and does not ask the other to do anything unsafe.
[[Provider]] holds any licence, registration or insurance that this agreement says the work needs, and shows it on request.
If [[provider]] cancels, or does not attend, [[engager]] gets back everything paid for the cancelled work within 14 days.
A party who does not attend without telling the other is recorded on SnapLink as a no-show, unless their reason is accepted through SnapLink’s dispute route.
Each party keeps private any personal details they learn about the other through this booking, and uses them only to carry it out, as UK data protection law requires.
No one is filmed or photographed for publication without their consent.

The work counts as done when [[provider]] has carried out the duties set out in this agreement. Either party may record evidence of this through SnapLink, where it is kept privately and not published.
A disagreement about this agreement goes first to SnapLink’s dispute route, and both parties take part in it in good faith before going elsewhere.
This agreement is governed by the law of [[jurisdiction]], and [[courts]] may decide any claim about it.

SnapLink keeps the signed version, the signature records and the terms hash that identifies this exact text. The terms hash may be recorded on a public blockchain; no name, address, pay or other personal detail is recorded there.
Where [[provider]] is registered for VAT, VAT is added to the fee at the rate in force when it is invoiced.
[[Provider]] is responsible for their own income tax and National Insurance on the fee.
If [[engager]] pays late, [[provider]] may claim interest and compensation under the Late Payment of Commercial Debts (Interest) Act 1998.

Either party may cancel by message through SnapLink. If [[engager]] cancels less than {{notice_hours}} hours before the start, {{late_cancellation_share}} of the fee is due to [[provider]] as a fair estimate of their loss.
[[Engager]] gives [[provider]] the safety information for the venue, and any site induction it needs, before the start.
[[Provider]] keeps confidential any non-public information about [[engager]]’s products, campaigns or plans that they learn through this booking, until it is made public other than by them.
If [[engager]] raises no problem within 7 days of the work being completed, the work is treated as accepted.
